name: Freddie Gebbett
headline: Ops generalist at Lawhive, one of the UK's fastest-growing AI startups, with a top-of-team B2B sales record behind me. I run operations, events and partnerships, and I pick up whatever doesn't have an owner yet. Looking for a founders or ops associate role at a seed or Series A startup. More at fwg.fyi.

roles.title: Office & Engagement Manager (Operations)
roles.siteBlurb: I keep a fast-moving legal-tech team running and the culture sharp: operations, the office, and the day-to-day that lets everyone do their best work.
bullets: Own operations at one of the UK's fastest-growing AI startups: the office, suppliers, budgets, invoices and expenses, contracts, events and partnerships. Started the company run club along the way.

Ran the office move as a project from start to finish: scoped it, ran the supplier process, reviewed the lease and negotiated 17% off list price and a 2-year fixed term instead of the 5 years on the table.

Built our benefits package from a blank page, learning broking and salary sacrifice from scratch: modelled the costs, ran the private medical tender across Bupa, AXA and Vitality, negotiated a 2-year platform fee waiver with Kota, and wrote the board proposal that got it approved. Set up salary sacrifice with payroll, wrote the policies and handled the confidential salary and medical data.
Support hiring: screen candidates, coordinate interviews and onboard new joiners.

Ran Lawhive's AI hackathon for 100 people from start to finish, on making the law more accessible. Did the sponsor outreach myself and ran those conversations through to a yes: GV, Balderton, Lovable and Anthropic all sponsored.

Built our office hub myself (90+ releases, no engineer) to get the team using the office together: a question of the day on the office screens, a beer vote, a shared playlist, aircon and 3D print requests. Automated the repeat admin with n8n and Claude, and documented the processes.

roles.title: Client Acquisition Manager
bullets: Hired to book meetings, moved into full-cycle B2B sales within three months: 21% close rate, top closed MRR on the team.
Top meeting volume every month across UK & Ireland (10-15 a week), running my own pipeline in the CRM.
Stepped across to the commercial arm (TNW Energy) to own a full sales cycle: prospected, booked and closed Custom Solar, one of the UK's largest commercial solar installers.

roles.title: Outreach Associate (SDR)
bullets: First job out of university: 150% of call quota, 133% of meeting quota, MVP award three months running.

Worked with the MD on the accountant-partner channel. Designed a new outbound email process to accountant partners and lifted engagement by 15%, the first time I designed a process rather than ran one.
Set the company record for accountant-partner meetings booked and attended in a month (7 of 8), 113% over quota.

builds.name: Inkly
builds.blurb: One booking link for tattoo artists: clients see the work, book a piece and pay the deposit up front, so the Instagram-DM admin and the no-shows both disappear.
cvBullets: Building one booking link for tattoo artists, solo from product to payments, brand and front end: portfolio, booking and deposits in one, replacing the Instagram-DM admin that costs artists their evenings and their no-shows.

builds.name: Annabel AI
builds.blurb: An AI receptionist for dentists, answering calls and booking patients when the front desk was busy or closed. My brother and I ran it together for three months: he owned the engineering, I owned everything that got it into practices.
builds.coda: Loved building it and learned a lot. Turns out AI voice agents are pretty competitive in 2026.

cvBullets: Co-founded a three-month AI voice-receptionist venture for UK dental practices with my brother: he built it, I took it to market. 10+ practices onboarded across three London boroughs, 1,000+ calls answered, 100+ appointments booked.

Owned go-to-market: ICP, market and competitor research, positioning, the pricing model, brand, website, all outbound and customer onboarding. Learned enough of the stack to hold my own on product calls.
Called it after three months when the market got crowded. The full story is on fwg.fyi.
